Ali brought water in his shield and Fatima washed the blood from the Prophet's face, then the ash of a burnt straw mat filled his wound.
Companions refused hospitality recite Al-Fatiha as Ruqya over a stung chief for a flock of sheep, and the Prophet approves and asks for a share.
Ali brought water in his shield, Fatima washed the blood from the Prophet's face, and ash from a burnt palm mat was put into his wound.
Plague was a punishment on Israelites or earlier people and a mercy for believers: do not enter or flee a plague land, and one staying patiently gets a martyr's reward.
Visiting a sick bedouin, the Prophet wished him a cure; when the man said his fever would take him to the grave, he replied: may it be as you say.
The Kam'a fungus is like manna, and its water is a cure for eye trouble.
The Prophet said al-kam'a is like manna and its water cures eye disease.
When a relative died, Aisha had talbina served to the women, citing the Prophet's saying that talbina soothes the patient's heart and eases some sadness.
Visit the sick, feed the hungry and free captives, the Prophet ordered; he and Abu Bakr walked to visit the unconscious Jabir, reviving him with his ablution water.
Aisha visited the feverish Abu Bakr and Bilal; the Prophet visited a dying grandchild, a sick bedouin, a Jewish boy who embraced Islam and Sa'd, and was visited when ill.
Patients spoke of their pain: Ka'b's lice, Aisha's headache, the Prophet's high fever, and Sa'd's illness, when the Prophet said giving a third in charity was too much.
Allah created treatment for every disease; women on expeditions brought back the wounded; healing is in honey, cupping and cautery, which the Prophet disliked; honey cured abdominal trouble.
Black cumin heals every disease except death, talbina comforts the sick and grieving, and Indian incense treats seven diseases; the Prophet was cupped, paid the cupper and used snuff.
The Prophet was cupped while fasting and in ihram, on his head, paid the cupper and forbade pressing children's tonsils; Ka'b was told to shave his lice-ridden head and expiate.
Truffle water heals the eyes; the Prophet had those who forced medicine into his mouth take it, had seven water-skins poured on him, and prescribed Indian incense and honey.
Indian incense cures seven diseases; Ruqya was allowed for poison and ear ailment; Anas was cauterised; Fatima's ash stopped the Prophet's bleeding; fever, from Hell's heat, is cooled with water.
Do not enter or flee a plague-struck land, as Abdur-Rahman told Umar; plague will not enter Medina, and dying of it or enduring it patiently brings a martyr's reward.
The Prophet blew the Mu'auwidhat over himself when ill; Al-Fatiha recited as Ruqya earned sheep he approved; Ruqya treats the evil eye and stings, invoking the Lord of the people.
At bedtime the Prophet recited Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas and blew on his palms, wiping his body, as Aisha did for him when ill; Al-Fatiha cured a stung chief.
Seven Ajwa dates guard against magic and poison; fanged beasts are forbidden as food; a fly falling in a vessel is dipped wholly, one wing bearing disease, the other healing.
Allah sent plague as punishment on whom He willed but made it mercy for believers: whoever patiently stays in a stricken town, accepting what Allah wrote, earns a martyr's reward.
Umar turned back from Sargh on hearing the Prophet's saying, from Abdur-Rahman, not to enter a plague-stricken land nor flee one, plague being a punishment sent on nations.
